title: Donut slice gaps hide tiny positive segments

complexity.rationale: The fixed-stroke root cause is confirmed, but the minimum-visibility and separator policy for infeasibly small arcs still requires a product and implementation decision.

summary: S2 Donut segments with very small positive values can disappear when rendered beside a dominant segment. The fixed background-colored slice-gap stroke can consume the entire visible fill of a narrow arc, leaving apparent white space instead of a sliver.
symptom: With one dominant value and many tiny positive values, the dominant arc does not visibly transition through the expected colored slivers. Some or all of the tiny segments appear as blank background-colored space even though their values are nonzero.
rootCause: packages/vega-spec-builder-s2/src/donut/donutUtils.ts:155-181 applies the fixed `${name}_sliceGap` signal as a centered background-colored `strokeWidth` on every arc. packages/constants/constants.ts:246-249 defines normal size-tier gaps of up to 2px. When a positive segment's angular width produces less than that visible arc length, the stroke covers its fill and makes the segment appear absent. The pie transform and derived angles in packages/vega-spec-builder-s2/src/donut/donutSpecBuilder.ts:135-157 preserve the tiny values correctly; there is no small-value filter or minimum-angle rule. S1 does not reproduce this encoding because packages/vega-spec-builder/src/donut/donutUtils.ts:62-78 uses zero normal stroke width and an angular pad instead.

comparison.expected: Every positive segment remains visibly represented, or a documented fallback such as aggregation is applied when individual segments cannot be rendered.
comparison.actual: A fixed pixel-width background stroke can cover the complete fill of a tiny arc, making valid positive segments appear missing.

comparison.expected: S2 preserves its intended separator appearance without erasing segments that remain visible in the equivalent S1 geometry.
comparison.actual: S1 uses an angular pad with no normal stroke, while S2 centers a fixed background stroke on every arc regardless of the arc's available width.

edgeCases.case: One dominant segment with many values between 1 and 12
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Tiny positive categories remain distinguishable or follow the documented minimum-size fallback rather than appearing as unexplained white space.

edgeCases.case: A tiny segment whose outer arc length is smaller than the configured slice gap
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The effective separator does not exceed the available segment geometry.

edgeCases.case: XS through XL Donut size tiers
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The visibility policy remains consistent as the configured slice gap and radius change.

edgeCases.case: Hovered, selected, or legend-highlighted tiny segments
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Interaction strokes and opacity rules do not erase a segment that is otherwise visible.
The fix does not create artificial visible arcs for values that the existing pie semantics do not render.
Tiny-segment visibility and separator behavior are consistent across renderers.

crossCutting.notes: The baseline defect is in static S2 arc geometry. Existing hover, controlled-highlight, legend, tooltip, and popover paths do not cause it, though selected-stroke behavior should be covered by regression tests. The existing slice-gap signal and scale can be reused or replaced without requiring S1 parity; S1 uses different separation geometry and retains tiny fills.

implementationPlan.change: Replace the unconditional fixed separator stroke with geometry that cannot consume the complete fill of a positive arc, while preserving the intended S2 gap for ordinary segments and defining selected-stroke behavior for tiny arcs.
Add regression coverage for dominant-plus-sliver data that verifies tiny positive arcs retain valid geometry and that the chosen separator encoding is bounded by the available segment width.
implementationPlan.lines: existing donut transform and mark tests

implementationPlan.change: Retain the dominant-segment dataset as the visual regression scenario and document the expected tiny-segment rendering once the separator policy is selected.

openQuestions: Should extremely small positive values always receive a minimum visible width, use a clamped separator, or be aggregated into an `Other` segment?
Should S2 continue using a pixel stroke for separation or switch to an angular gap that scales with each segment?
Should the selected-item stroke also be reduced or suppressed when it would cover a tiny arc?
Does runtime rendering show any additional SVG or canvas anti-aliasing differences beyond the confirmed background-stroke coverage?
